claims.text: The starting material is a homogenized Al0.7CoCrFeNi eutectic alloy.
The starting alloy has a dual-phase lamellar FCC/B2 structure.
Incoherent lamellar interfaces cause stress concentration and brittleness in the starting alloy.
The proposed intervention is hexahedron-anvil HPHT treatment at approximately 6 GPa and 1473 K for 2 hours.
Treatment at 6 GPa and 1473 K for 2 hours will topologically transform the lamellar microstructure into a hierarchical pattern.
The HPHT treatment will replace incoherent FCC/B2 boundaries with coherent interfaces.
The proposed pressure and temperature are below the phase-instability, decomposition, or melting threshold of the FCC/B2 eutectic.
Coherent interfaces facilitate dislocation transfer across boundaries.
Shockley partial dislocations and perfect dislocations can transfer between the FCC and B2 phases through the proposed coherent interfaces.
The hierarchical coherent structure will activate dislocation transfer, stacking faults, and twinning.
Dislocation transfer across coherent interfaces will reduce interfacial stress concentration and make strain distribution more homogeneous.
More homogeneous strain distribution will prevent microcracks from coalescing along phase interfaces.
At high strain, the GND densities of the FCC and B2 phases will converge after HPHT treatment.
The treated specimen will show elongated crack propagation rather than isolated microcracks.
The HPHT treatment will significantly increase ductility without sacrificing strength.
The baseline alloy exhibits isolated microcracks.
The baseline alloy exhibits strong strain localization in the FCC phase near phase boundaries.
The baseline alloy has divergent GND densities between its FCC and B2 phases.

contradictions.description: The mechanism says the treatment prevents microcrack coalescence, whereas the predicted outcome favors elongated crack propagation over isolated microcracks. Elongated interfacial cracks would ordinarily indicate crack propagation or coalescence, making the proposed favorable fracture-morphology criterion internally ambiguous.
